Reading your comments in this thread, it seems to me that you are a proponent of the Perennial Philosophy, whether you recognize it or not. It's a particularly pacifistic "way of life" that points out how all, or most major worldly religions all share elements that point to the central tenet of ego-death and joining the Oneness of the universe / eternity by renouncing the temporal completely. Properly stated, it is a worldview that gets a lot right, but it also makes many mistakes.

Fundamental to the Perennial Philosophy is its pacifism; by believing that only the Eternal really matters, the Perennial Philosopher rejects that any of the suffering in the temporal realm is meaningful, and so he cares not about being charitable or "wasting energy" on helping others, because the real concern is focusing on the annihilation of his own ego. "Besides", he says, "those who suffer will just reincarnate again until they get it right!"

It is ultimately very flawed in its understanding of soul and the temporal. We don't have many lives or many souls, but one life and one soul. We can't all be mediators between man and God by virtue of achieving ego-death; reaching or touching eternity does not grant Godhead. We therefore depend on the Godhead coming down to us to act as that Mediator. Only Christianity offers this.

Thus using "Jesus" as a way to entice people into your ultimately Christ-less Perennial Philosophy is disingenuous. Jesus is not just "another example" of love; He is Love, the ideal that all others approach, whether they lived before Him or after.

Yes, love is the answer, but you have to be responsible in your understanding of it, and know that the actions you perform in this world do matter, even if ultimately this world matters not.
